column1: # divergences are expected, ruled, and gated explicitly): one row per known
# dartq-vs-oracle divergence face of a package:lints rule, consolidating the
# per-rule approximation doc-comments of crates/dartq-lints (audit lints-r1
# finding F6) into one machine-readable table. A rule may carry several rows
# -- one per divergence face (avoid_types_as_parameter_names appears twice):
# multi-face rows are legal; the gate preflight matches rows, not rules.
#   rule        lowercase SDK machine name (same form as lint_codes.txt)
#   face        the divergence face, one line, no tabs
#               under-reports) | structural (cannot appear on both sides)
#               diffs are real bugs) | fixed (historical). Retirement
#               fixture for the rule exists under tests/corpus/lints AND
#               one full lint-gate cycle has passed green after it — until
#               both hold, the row stays for provenance.
#   citation    rule module (file + module name, grep-stable — no line
#               numbers, they rot on every edit), or audit/SDK anchor
# Consistency pin: scripts/lint-gate.sh preflight asserts every `excluded`
# row is absent from lint_codes.txt, every `in_universe` row is present in
# it, and every vendored-set rule missing from lint_codes.txt carries an
# `excluded` row here — the ledger and the frozen universe cannot drift.
# Spelling pin: the ledger and lint_codes.txt carry the SDK machine-name
# with "(pinned as <module name>)"; do not normalize the spellings — the
# lint-gate preflight and the registry pin match on the SDK machine name.
# Sweep status (closed 2026-10-13): the approximation-doc sweep promised by
# the seed rows is complete — every rule module's approximation
# doc-comments under crates/dartq-lints/src/rules/*.rs were walked. Every
# rule whose docs state a dartq-vs-oracle divergence face carries a row
# (the 2026-10-13 sweep block below; the seed block keeps its original
# order). Rules whose docs state only behavior-preserving approximations
# or agreement carry no row (e.g. unnecessary_null_aware_assignments: the
# setter-exclusion shape matches the official's writeElement verdict on
# Reconciliation (#1715, 2026-10-16): every row's citation now leads with a
# reconciliation tag stating the burn state of its divergence face, ruled
# against three fresh evidence sources (priority order): (1)
# ledger, 212 entries as of the #1715 reconciliation and 217 now (the 212
# case-sorted entries plus the 5 tail sentinel class rows), all
# parser/semantic codes and zero lint-rule rows, so it retires nothing
# run, the measured per-rule per-file (code,file) direction authority;
# (3) the worktree's pin tests under crates/dartq-lints — a pinned face is
# fixed-and-locked, cited by grep-stable test name. Tags are
# `#<ticket>/<face-state>`: the ticket prefix is the reconciliation wave
# that ruled the state (#1715 seeded the scheme; later reconciliation
# waves reuse the vocabulary under their own ticket prefix). The
#   open                still divergent: a w3-measured face, or a standing
#                       approximation face the rule module's doc-comments
#                       state; direction corrected where w3 contradicts.
#   fixed-pinned        retired from burn; the citation names the pin
#                       test(s). gate_status=fixed where the whole face set
#                       closed; in_universe where the row doubles as a live
#   in-flight           the rule's home file is mid-burn under a named
#                       lane; the row re-reconciles post-lane — the
#                       measured w3 direction is recorded in the citation
#                       so the lanes inherit it. (All #1715 lanes closed;
#                       no current row carries this state.)
#   retired-stale       no divergence face exists in any evidence
#   burned              the cited face closed in the named burn lane; the
#                       citation's pins are that lane's burn evidence.
#   burned-pins         the lane landed pins for its faces while the
#   narrowed            a partial burn: the cited face closed, the
#                       residual faces keep the row in_universe.
# Direction-reversal audit (TSV vs the w3 measurement): recursive_getters,
# unnecessary_getters_setters and type_init_formals said dartq_only but
# measured oracle_only; prefer_initializing_formals said oracle_only but
# measured dartq_only — all four closed or re-faced below. Two further
# reversals sat on in-flight rows and were recorded on them (both rows
# re-reconciled post-lane, directions corrected on the rows):
# Seed rows (the initial triage sweep + the #721 main-agent rulings).
